{{nihongo|'''Sugiyama Shrine'''|杉山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Sugiyama Shrine''' (すぎやまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kōhoku-ku, Yokohama|Q1358965|qid=Q1358965}}, {{ill|Yokohama|Q38283|qid=Q38283}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|Q127513|qid=Q127513}}. It was the former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} of Yoshida in old {{ill|Nitta|Q11503739|qid=Q11503739|lt=Nitta Village}}, and is regarded as one of the strong candidate shrines for "{{ill|Sukiyamano Shrine|Q135039726|qid=Q135039726}}," the only shikinaisha in Yokohama and in former {{ill|Musashi Province|ar|محافظة موساشي|ca|Província de Musashi|ckb|پارێزگای موساشی|cs|Provincie Musaši|de|Provinz Musashi|eo|Provinco Musaŝi|es|Provincia de Musashi|fa|ولایت موساشی|fr|Province de Musashi|gl|Provincia de Musashi|hak|Musashi-koet|id|Provinsi Musashi|it|Musashi (provincia)|ja|武蔵国|ko|무사시국|lt|Musašio žemė|nl|Musashi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Musashi|pt|Província de Musashi|ru|Мусаси (провинция)|simple|Musashi Province|sk|Musaši (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мусаши|th|แคว้นมูซาชิ|tr|Musashi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мусаші|vi|Musashi (tỉnh)|zh|武藏國|zh_min_nan|Musasi-kok|zh_yue|武藏國|qid=Q907398}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}} (Iso-takeru)
* {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|lt=Co-enshrined}}: {{ill|Kamakura Gongorō Kagemasa|Q1154948|qid=Q1154948|lt=Gongorō Kagemasa}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hino Seibyō}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}<ref name="kamnavi-shinyoshida-sugiyama">[http://kamnavi.jp/it/musasi/indexy.htm#khayabu1 Musashi's Isotakeru no Mikoto, Shin-yoshida-chō Sugiyama Shrine] (Kamnavi)</ref>
*: In {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 41), three shrines in Nitta village were {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyama (shinyoshida)">[http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=176&cd=1202081&scd=&npg=0 Sugiyama Shrine] (Kanagawa Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines)</ref>.

=== Origin and history ===
There is a theory that it was worshipped by a clan that moved from {{ill|Bōsō Peninsula|Q1022115|qid=Q1022115}}<ref name="kamnavi-shinyoshida-sugiyama"/>. Its founding time is unknown. ''Musashi Shikishaki'' states, "In Tsuzuki District, at the place called Yoshida, there is a small place-name Sugiyama, and the shrine there is the true site." ''{{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|Q11503943|qid=Q11503943}}'' (compiled in the Bunka-Bunsei period, 1804-1829) records: "Tax-exempt land 2 dan 5 se; to the north of the village; several stone steps up to a torii before the shrine; main shrine 2 ken by 2.5 ken; haiden 3 ken by 2 ken, south-facing; sacred body immovable; held by Shōfuku-ji in the village"<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyama (shinyoshida)"/> {{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō Yoshida Village}}. Sacred treasures and historical documents of this shrine had been kept by Shōfuku-ji, its former {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}, but are said to have been completely lost in a fire at that temple<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama">[http://www18.ocn.ne.jp/~tugaru/sikinaisyasugiyama.html Inference on Sugiyama Shrine, the only shikinaisha of Musashi Tsuzuki District] (Tsugaru Ancient Kingdom)</ref>.

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), it was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} in then Tsuzuki District's Yoshida Village (which became Nitta Village in the 1889 merger)<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyama (shinyoshida)"/>.

=== As a shikinaisha candidate ===
The theory identifying this shrine as the shikinaisha predates the Bunka-Bunsei period when ''Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō'' was compiled. Works such as ''Historical Geography of Musashi Shikinaisha'' by late-Edo Shinto scholar Saitō Yoshihiko and local historian Hishinuma Isamu (published 1966, revised 1972 as ''Ancient Shrines of Musashi'') treat this theory as strong<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku52/ History and Culture of Kōhoku Ward: 52nd article, strong candidate for Sugiyama Shrine] (Ōkura Institute for Spiritual Culture)</ref>. Hishinuma cited the existence of a local minor place-name "Sugiyama," oral tradition in the long-established Mori family connected to this shrine claiming over 1,000 years of history, and a kofun called Asamazuka behind the Mori residence indicating a once-powerful local clan. ''History of Kōhoku Ward'' also says the Mori family name derives from "chinju-no-mori" and that the family is locally called "Sugiyama-sama"<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku53/ History and Culture of Kōhoku Ward: 53rd article, Sugiyama shrines in the ward] (Ōkura Institute for Spiritual Culture)</ref>. Nearby in Hayabuchi 3-chōme are the Kitagawa Omote-no-Ue site and {{ill|Kitagawa Shell Mound|Q11401676|qid=Q11401676}}, and local memory of a "Kaizuka-batake" aligns with the ''Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō'' note that there was a large shell mound in Tsuzuki District Yoshida village{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō Yoshida Village}}, showing ancient sites in this area have long been known<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama"/>.

Like many other candidate shrines, this shrine stands on elevated ground along the {{ill|Tsurumi River|Q7850292|qid=Q7850292}} system ({{ill|Hayabuchi River|Q11511423|qid=Q11511423}}).

=== Other ===
No priest is stationed permanently at this shrine; it is managed concurrently by [http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=359&cd=1203043&scd=000&npg=0 Hachiman-sha] in Setogaya-chō, Hodogaya Ward.

=== Location and access ===
4509 Shin-yoshida-chō, Kōhoku Ward, Yokohama, Kanagawa Prefecture
* {{ill|Yokohama Municipal Subway Green Line|Q910329|qid=Q910329}}: 15-20 minutes on foot from {{ill|Higashi-Yamata Station|Q11103294|qid=Q11103294}}
